headline: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected as Bangladesh's 23rd president
summary: The Election Commission has issued a gazette declaring him president following a historic ballot, drawing congratulations from national and international leaders.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The Election Commission has officially issued a gazette notification declaring the result of the historic ballot.
Congratulations have poured in for the new president from various quarters, including Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, the Prime Minister, and other high-ranking government officials.
International leaders and representatives from China and the UK have also sent their congratulations to President-elect Fakhrul.
The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled to take place at Bangabhaban on Friday evening at 7:30 PM.
To ensure security and smooth movement, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has issued special traffic directives for the Bangabhaban area from 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM on Friday.

Traffic will be restricted on several roads, including the route from Motijheel Shapla Chattar to Dilkusha Commercial Area and Rajuk Crossing. Alternative routes have been advised for buses and commercial vehicles.
The ceremony will be attended by the outgoing president, the Prime Minister, the Speaker, the Chief Justice, former presidents, cabinet members, foreign diplomats, and other distinguished guests.
caption:
Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir is now the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The Election Commission has officially declared the result.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been elected as the 23rd President of Bangladesh. The Election Commission has officially issued a gazette notification declaring the result of the historic ballot.

Congratulations have poured in for the new president from various quarters, including Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, the Prime Minister, and other high-ranking government officials.

International leaders and representatives from China and the UK have also sent their congratulations to President-elect Fakhrul.

The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled to take place at Bangabhaban on Friday evening at 7:30 PM.

To ensure security and smooth movement, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has issued special traffic directives for the Bangabhaban area from 3:00 PM to 9:00 PM on Friday.

Traffic will be restricted on several roads, including the route from Motijheel Shapla Chattar to Dilkusha Commercial Area and Rajuk Crossing. Alternative routes have been advised for buses and commercial vehicles.

The ceremony will be attended by the outgoing president, the Prime Minister, the Speaker, the Chief Justice, former presidents, cabinet members, foreign diplomats, and other distinguished guests.

headline_marked: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi [[appointed BNP acting secretary general]]
headline: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi appointed BNP acting secretary general
summary: The appointment follows Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir's election as president and comes shortly after Rizvi's induction into the National Standing Committee.
details: Ruhul Kabir Rizvi has been appointed as the acting secretary general of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). The decision was announced in a press release yesterday, following the election of Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir as party president.
Rizvi's appointment comes just five days after he was inducted into the BNP's highest policymaking body, the National Standing Committee on August 15.

He previously served as the party's senior joint secretary general since 2016. Following the formation of the BNP government, he was appointed as an adviser to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman with the rank of a minister.

Born in Kurigram, Rizvi began his political career with the left-wing Biplobi Chhatra Union and later joined Chhatra Dal, rising to become the first leader elected as president of its central committee through a vote in 1992.

As a student leader, Rizvi was active in the movement against the military rule of HM Ershad. During the anti-autocracy movement, he suffered a spinal injury that left him with permanent physical disabilities.

Rizvi has been one of the BNP's most visible leaders, often briefing the media at the party's Nayapaltan headquarters while other leaders faced arrests. Party leaders state that over 180 cases were filed against him during that period.
caption:
